question: Does dense supervision of remaining original-document body fraction improve coherent natural completion, beyond unchanged native next-token CE, without modifying inference?
scope: A new independently defined matched25M-per-arm pilot for a distinct TRAIN-only scalar target. Not a change/relaunch/teacher rescue of any closed100M condition. The full four-item goal still requires a qualified main recipe, genuinely fresh whole-pipeline seed43/fullDEV/all440/new sealedTEST/adoption. Pilot completion is never overall success.
rationale: Observed raw loops and low appropriate completion remain despite CE/grammar improvements; original-LF counterfactual showed a local boundary cue but did not establish the semantic root cause. A dense progress target is a different auxiliary planning signal. Neither local observation nor external paper proves a benefit.

recipe.auxiliary: mean abs(sigmoid(w dot final_native_normalized_hidden)-remaining_original_body_fraction) at exactly selected main slots
recipe.inference: Original native full/fast/cache/vocabulary softmax and fixed greedy policy, no progress-head access/stop rule/length hint/normalization
recipe.main: Original unweighted next-token mean CE, every original selected body/EOS target and context unchanged
recipe.remaining_fraction: For N original body tokens, current hidden absolute serialized input position j=input_start+physical_column, target=(N-j)/N. BOS j0 gives1; last original body jN predicting original EOS gives0. Overlap/PAD/quota-masked targets excluded; fragment/window end never made a terminal event.
recipe.head: One fresh zero-initialized no-bias FP32 scalar linear head, hidden_size weights, train-only and absent at inference

teachers.label_scope: Scalar progress labels are additional supervision, separately counted; not additional vocabulary targets or free teacher compute.

initialization: Both arms copy original10B model and start fresh same AdamW/source seed. Both contain same zero train-only scalar head; head construction uses zeros and does not advance CPU/CUDA RNG. Control computes head loss times0 and clips original coordinate list only to prove native reduction order. Candidate clips all actual trainable coordinates. No original weight reparameterization.
control: Train NEW native_CE_control25M under same goals/cursors/row order as NEW candidate25M. Cached native CE100M is a separately labeled reference, never a matched25M control. Compare full source sampler/digest/teacher/EOS/byte/physical clocks between new arms, preserve original absolute/strong/historical/native100M guards.

training.optimizer: Fresh AdamW1e-5 WD.1 betas.9/.999 eps1e-8 constant clip1
training.material: Same accepted original TRAIN/Tokenizer/index-byte selector/document windows. No new corpus, synthetic EOS, prefix-suffix reordering or special tokens.

novelty.middle_CE: Old original-vocabulary current-target CE at middle layer. New scalar non-vocabulary target from final native hidden, no shared early-head supervision.
novelty.FIM: No FIM transformation, marker or right context; this is explicitly a left-to-right original-document adaptation, not HLP reproduction or reopening a FIM recipe.
novelty.search: Bounded original source/test/proposal/completion/review searches for HLP, horizon-length, remaining fraction/body/length, countdown, document progress and length prediction found no such trained scalar objective. Original next-two/middle/document-weighting sources inspected; search absence alone is not exhaustive novelty proof.
novelty.document_balance: Old inverse-document-length weights change existing CE weighting; here every original CE term retains equal weight and a separately counted scalar objective is added.
novelty.negative_evidence: EOS positional attractors in external analysis caution that teaching progress could harm generalization. Keep all original quality/length suites and do not claim a diagnosed planning deficit.
novelty.EOS_weight: No EOS/nonEOS relabeling, unigram calibration or stop postprocessing. Labels are dense original remaining fraction, not a direct inference stop decision.
novelty.next_two: Old train-only contextual Block predicts the next-next vocabulary ID. New scalar head predicts original-document progress over varying horizons from metadata, with no extra Block/norm/decoder invocation. Not a changed horizon/coefficient/head rescue of next-two.

literature.title: Horizon-Length Prediction: Advancing Fill-in-the-Middle Capabilities for Code Generation with Lookahead Planning
literature.used: Normalized remaining fraction, sigmoid linear head, L1, lambda.1, train-only head
literature.limits: Code FIM with prefix+suffix and1.3B-7B models, not Japanese10M L2R or proof that document length teaches semantic planning. Our BOS-inclusive original-document target and zero head initialization are explicitly an adaptation.
